trigger: When planning dev task lanes
lesson: Never put tests/e2e/**, tests/acceptance/**, docs/** or .forge/** in a dev task's lanes or acceptance; QA owns e2e and devs can't write there.

trigger: When reviewing a task
lesson: Judge only the task's lanes plus tests/unit; never reject for missing files the developer is not allowed to write.

trigger: When the same gate error comes back after a fix
lesson: Stop and report BLOCKED with the exact cause and file, instead of retrying the same kind of fix.

trigger: When finishing contracts and stubs
lesson: Run `npm run check` after your last edit; main must stay green after the baseline commit or the contract gate fails.

trigger: When writing Playwright specs
lesson: Run `npx tsc --noEmit` on new e2e files before finishing; a spec that breaks typecheck is reverted and wastes the round.

trigger: When a lint or config error outside your lanes blocks the gate
lesson: Report it as a concern; don't edit eslint, tsconfig or vite configs that are not in your lanes.

trigger: when running shell commands or reading files from inside the task worktree
lesson: Use paths relative to your working directory root and never climb with ../ to reach shared files such as src/shared/contracts.ts; if a file is outside your directory, report it instead of trying other relative paths.
note: Learned from guard false positives: the guard read ../ imports inside heredoc file contents as paths. Guard fixed; relative imports are correct.

trigger: when drafting or revising docs/prd.json from a brief
lesson: Map every requirement in the brief to a PRD item before finishing, and add must-haves only when the brief or an explicit requirement asks for them.

trigger: when you need git status, diff or log while working in a task worktree
lesson: Run git commands only inside your own task worktree; if you need repository-wide history or another branch, report it instead of running git from a parent or shared path.

trigger: when building a page or control that the brief or docs/design.md specifies
lesson: Implement the exact control state (disabled versus hidden) and screen composition that the brief and docs/design.md name, and check each one against the brief before reporting DONE.

trigger: when producing docs/design.md under a turn or dollar budget
lesson: Write docs/design.md early in incremental sections and stop exploring once half the budget is used, so a usable file exists before the cap is hit.

trigger: when writing notes, placeholders or scratch files while drafting the PRD
lesson: Keep scratch files inside the run's writable directory and never write to /tmp, because writes outside it are denied and waste a turn.

trigger: when a contract or stub change seems to need a file your role cannot write, such as a UI component
lesson: Do not touch or read-probe files your role cannot write, such as UI components; record the needed change as a note in the contract handoff for the owning role.

trigger: when a Bash command is denied by the guard as outside your working directory
lesson: Do not retry or probe a ../ path that the guard denied as outside your working directory; use only files inside your worktree and report any missing shared file as a concern.

trigger: when writing unit tests for layout or styling changes
lesson: Assert behavior or a single source of truth for layout instead of regex-matching exact Tailwind class strings across several files, so a spec change does not invalidate the test.

trigger: when planning a fix task whose bug may sit in shared contract or helper code
lesson: Include the shared file that holds the bug (for example src/shared/booking.ts) in the fix task's lanes instead of leaving it out, because a developer blocked by an out-of-lane file wastes a round.

trigger: when a Bash command is denied by the guard as outside your working directory
lesson: Do not retry or probe ../ paths the guard denied; read only files inside your working directory and record any missing shared file as a note in the contract handoff.

trigger: When choosing the visual direction for a consumer-facing app
lesson: Commit to one bold, high-contrast direction: a dark top bar with a single saturated accent used as solid plates (brand mark, prices, active nav, step numbers), a heavy, wide display face for headings, white cards on a light page, and real product photos. Avoid muted or pastel palettes, low-contrast grey-on-grey and anything that reads as a starter template.

trigger: When designing heroes, empty states and illustrations
lesson: Never draw illustrations (hand-made SVG scenes or clip art) for heroes or empty states: they look amateur. Use the product's own photos (e.g. the seeded listing images) or strong typography alone, and say so in docs/design.md so developers don't add one.

trigger: when writing a range or overlap check that compares a new request against stored records
lesson: Normalize both sides of an overlap comparison to the same boundary convention (end-exclusive or end-inclusive) and check the stored-record side as carefully as the new-request side before reporting DONE.

trigger: When writing session or auth cookie helpers
lesson: Never set secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === "production" on cookies. The Docker deploy runs NODE_ENV=production over plain http://localhost, and Safari drops Secure cookies on http (even localhost), so login succeeds but every later call is 401. Use secure: process.env.COOKIE_SECURE === "true" (off by default) and list COOKIE_SECURE in .env.example.

trigger: When setting or changing cookies
lesson: Don't tie the cookie Secure flag to NODE_ENV: the deployed container is production over plain http, and Safari then drops the cookie (login works, everything after is 401; Chrome on localhost hides the bug). Keep secure behind COOKIE_SECURE=true.

trigger: When proving a deploy with login
lesson: After the container starts, prove a real session over http, not just /api/health: log in as a seeded user with curl -c jar, then curl -b jar /api/auth/me must be 200. A Secure cookie over http fails this check, and that's the bug Safari users hit.
